messages.subject: [R-sig-genetics] Advanced QGIS Spatial Analysis for Genetics
messages.subject_clean: Advanced QGIS Spatial Analysis for Genetics
messages.body_plain:
Hello R-SIG-GENETICS members

A reminder - Connect genetic data to the geographic context shaping sampled populations. Advanced QGIS: Spatial Analysis 2.0 is a 2-day seminar livestreaming August 11?12 with Nick Bearman (University College London and Geospatial Training Solutions). Spatial overlays, point-in-polygon operations, and coordinate-based data integration support rigorous analysis of geographic genetic patterns. Learn to join diverse datasets, conduct access analyses, and aggregate spatial results into meaningful metrics. Apply QGIS methods to relate sampling locations and spatial context to genetic research questions.

Details and registration: https://instats.org/seminar/advanced-qgis-spatial-analysis-20
Further information is available on the seminar page.


Best wishes

Michael Zyphur
Professor and Director

messages.subject: [R-sig-genetics] Online course. Invasion Genomics in R. 12-14-16 October
messages.subject_clean: Online course. Invasion Genomics in R. 12-14-16 October
messages.body_plain:
Dear all,

Registrations are open for our online course ?Invasion Genomics in R?, taking place 12, 14 & 16 October.
 
Course website: [ https://www.physalia-courses.org/courses-workshops/invasion-genomics/ ]( https://www.physalia-courses.org/courses-workshops/invasion-genomics/ ) 
 
Designed to foster international participation, the course combines recorded lectures, self-paced practical tutorials with annotated R scripts, and live remote instructor support. Participants can progress through the materials at their own pace while having the opportunity to ask questions and discuss challenges with the instructor. The format is particularly suited to participants across different time zones.
 
The course provides a practical introduction to invasion genomics, focusing on three key themes:
Movement dynamics ? investigating invasion sources, dispersal pathways, genetic diversity, and population structure
Adaptation dynamics ? applying selection outlier detection methods to investigate adaptive processes
Environmental adaptation ? using genotype-by-environment association (GEA) methods to explore how environmental conditions shape adaptive outcomes
The course is aimed at graduate students, researchers, and professionals interested in applying genomic approaches to invasion biology. 

Includes: Recorded lectures, guided practicals, annotated R scripts, and live remote support
Participants will gain both fundamental knowledge and practical experience to help them apply invasion genomic approaches in their own research.
 
For the full list of our courses and workshops, please visit: [ https://www.physalia-courses.org/courses-workshops/ ]( https://www.physalia-courses.org/courses-workshops/ )
 
 
 
Best regards,
 
Carlo

messages.subject: [R-sig-genetics] Genomics for Ecological and Evolutionary Studies
messages.subject_clean: Genomics for Ecological and Evolutionary Studies
messages.body_plain:
Hello R-SIG-GENETICS members

Develop practical genomic data skills for ecological and evolutionary research questions. Genomics for Ecological and Evolutionary Studies led by Giulio Formenti (Vertebrate Genome Lab, The Rockefeller University) and Guido Gallo (Department of Biosciences, University of Milan) is now available as an on-demand streaming seminar. Sequencing-data analysis and bioinformatics workflows can help genetics researchers connect genomic evidence to ecological and evolutionary questions. Participants practise obtaining public data, aligning short and long reads, calling variants, inspecting variant files, and comparing alignments with command-line tools. These methods can be applied alongside R-based genetic-data analysis to evaluate sequencing technologies, manage genomic datasets, and investigate biodiversity and evolutionary history.

Course details: https://instats.org/seminar/genomics-for-ecological-and-evolutionary-1
Further information is available on the Instats course page.


Best wishes

Michael Zyphur
Professor and Director

messages.subject: [R-sig-genetics] Appraising quantitative research in genetics
messages.body_plain:
Hello R-SIG-GENETICS members

Genetic analyses are easier to assess when claims, designs, and evidence remain aligned. Appraising and Improving Quantitative Research led by Centre for Applied Statistics Courses (CASC) (University College London) is now available as an on-demand streaming seminar. Critical appraisal of study design, bias, model assumptions, and sensitivity analyses can strengthen genetic data-analysis decisions. Learn to align research questions, estimands, sampling, and analytical choices while evaluating reported uncertainty and causal claims. Apply reproducibility checks, reporting frameworks, and transparent workflows when reviewing or improving quantitative genetics research in R.

Course details: https://instats.org/seminar/appraising-and-improving-quantitative-re-1
The course page includes the curriculum and enrollment details.


Best wishes

Michael Zyphur
Professor and Director

A reminder - Bring geographic context into genetic data analysis and presentation. Introduction to Spatial Data and R as a GIS 2.0 is a 2-day seminar livestreaming August 18?19 with Nick Bearman (University College London and Geospatial Training Solutions). Import, process, and visualise spatial data in R with sf, choropleth mapping, and map customisation. messages.subject: [R-sig-genetics] AI for Quantitative Qualitative Research
messages.body_plain:
Hello R-SIG-GENETICS members

Extend your R-based analyses with transparent, reproducible computational methods. AI for Quantitative & Qualitative Research led by Hadi Fariborzi (Bissett School of Business, Mount Royal University, Calgary) is now available as an on-demand streaming seminar. Build reproducible Python and R workflows for cleaning structured and text data, running regression, multilevel models, and structural equation models, and interpreting results with AI-assisted support. Apply replication checks and transparent code-to-results documentation to genetic data analyses while auditing generated code and model outputs for methodological soundness. Use thematic coding, text mining, and exportable notebooks to connect quantitative and qualitative evidence in collaborative research projects.

Course details: https://instats.org/seminar/ai-for-quantitative-and-qualitative-rese-1
Please circulate this information if it is relevant to colleagues or students.


Best wishes

messages.subject: [R-sig-genetics] Causal Machine Learning for Genetics
messages.body_plain:
Hello R-SIG-GENETICS members

Genetic data analysis can require clearer separation of association and causal effect. Causal Machine Learning led by Melvyn Weeks (Faculty of Economics, University of Cambridge) is now available as an on-demand streaming seminar. Use lasso, double lasso, double machine learning, and causal forests to distinguish causal effects from predictive associations. Genetics researchers can apply these approaches in R when investigating treatment effects or high-dimensional data alongside established identification strategies. Worked notebooks and sample data support replication and interpretation within a causal-inference workflow.

Course details: https://instats.org/seminar/causal-machine-learning-1
The course page includes the curriculum and enrollment details.


Best wishes

Michael Zyphur

messages.subject: [R-sig-genetics] New open-access AI readiness toolkit for universities
messages.subject_clean: New open-access AI readiness toolkit for universities
messages.body_plain:
Hello?everyone

I'm sharing a new open-access resource that you may find useful: The Institutional AI Readiness Pack <https://instats.org/publications/the-institutional-ai-readiness-pack> and its accompanying instruments catalogue <https://mzyphur.github.io/ai-readiness/instruments.html>.?

Universities increasingly have AI policies, but many still lack an evidence-based picture of how AI is actually used and governed across their research environments. Without that picture, they cannot reliably identify gaps across policy, people, systems, and process, nor can they determine how to strengthen the institutional capabilities that enable rigorous and responsible AI use in research. That is the gap this pack closes.?

The pack accompanies Responsible AI in Academic Research: A Competency Framework for Research Training <https://instats.org/publications/responsible-ai-in-academic-research>, which defines five dimensions of institutional readiness and the capabilities that underpin them. It turns that framework into an institutional self-assessment, surveys for graduate students and supervisors, gap-analysis and action-planning tools, model policy and disclosure materials, agreements, and briefings for university leaders. Every instrument is openly licensed under CC BY 4.0 and available in HTML, Word, and PDF.?

The framework is non-prescriptive about which maturity level an institution should occupy. Nobody outside your university is grading the exercise. There is no prize for a high score and no penalty for a low one. The real risk is relying on an inaccurate picture.?

For researchers, graduate students, and universities that want more structured training on AI in academic research, Instats is running a four-part seminar series <https://instats.org/course/agentic-ai-for-academic-research1> this month and next on how to understand and use AI for academic research. It covers AI as a Research Method, Responsible AI for Academic Research, Verifiable AI for Academic Research, and Building Agentic AI Research Teams. Each seminar stands alone, but together they provide a coherent progression for developing the knowledge and skills needed to use AI effectively for rigorous and honest research.

I hope you find the pack useful, and I hope you can join us for the seminar series. Please feel free to share both with students and colleagues working in research leadership, training, integrity, policy, or graduate education.


Best wishes

Michael Zyphur
Professor and Director
Instats |?instats.org <http://instats.org>

Hello R-SIG-GENETICS members

Build interpretable statistical workflows for genetic questions using R. Introduction to Bayesian Statistical Modelling 2.0 led by Rosina Savisaar (Mondego Science (Biostatistics)) is now available as an on-demand streaming seminar. Bayesian regression in R provides a framework for matching genetic data types to probability distributions and expressing prior information. Using brms, researchers can fit models, interpret posterior distributions, check model appropriateness, and visualize results. These skills can support genetic data analysis when evaluating uncertainty and making predictions.

Course details: https://instats.org/seminar/introduction-to-bayesian-statistical-mod-2
The full course outline is available on the Instats course page.

messages.subject: [R-sig-genetics] Causal Mediation Analysis in R
messages.body_plain:
Hello R-SIG-GENETICS members

Pathway questions demand more than estimating whether an association is present. Causal Mediation Analysis led by Paola Zaninotto (Epidemiology & Public Health, University College London) and Martin Danka (Centre for Longitudinal Studies, University College London) is now available as an on-demand streaming seminar. Counterfactual reasoning, g-computation, and interventional effects provide tools for examining causal pathways under complex confounding. Genetic-data researchers using R can apply these approaches to distinguish direct and mediated relationships while evaluating the assumptions behind their models. Practical implementation in R supports transparent estimation and interpretation of mediation effects in applied studies.

Course details: https://instats.org/seminar/causal-mediation-analysis-1
The course page includes the curriculum and enrollment details.


Best wishes

Michael Zyphur
Professor and Director
